title: Car Shield Exposed: Truth About Extended Warranty Lies And Huge Fines
summary: A consumer-advocate reporter covers the FTC's $10 million settlement with CarShield over deceptive extended-warranty advertising, including fake endorsements and overstated coverage.

assertions.quote: car Shield's ads deceptively feature consumer endorsers who claim to have saved a specific amount of money using their plans but have not

verdicts.note: Matches the FTC's 2023 settlement findings against CarShield and American Auto Shield.

FTC's complaint and $10M settlement found CarShield's ads and telemarketing deceptive, including that its celebrity endorsers (e.g. Ice-T) falsely claimed to have personally used and saved money with its service contracts.

assertions.quote: cari's Auto extended warranties cover all repairs or even repairs to the in quote covered Vehicle Systems instead the plans contain a myriad of exclusions

verdicts.note: A core finding of the FTC's complaint against CarShield.

FTC alleges CarShield ads claimed all repairs, or repairs to 'covered' systems, would be paid for, while in fact none of its VSCs covered all repairs and the plans contained myriad exclusions, so many were denied.

assertions.quote: many consumers with approved claims must pay a portion of the rental car cost

verdicts.note: Documented in the FTC complaint against CarShield.
FTC found CarShield ads promised a free rental car on breakdown, but consumers with denied claims got no rental car and many with approved claims still paid part of the cost.

assertions.quote: many consumers could not use the repair facility of their choice as many did not accept Auto extended warranties

verdicts.note: Documented in the FTC complaint against CarShield.
FTC found CarShield ads claimed customers could use the repair facility of their choice, but many shops did not accept CarShield's VSCs.
